messages.content: I made $85,000 last year. What would my tax be?

function.name: calculate_tax
function.description: Determines the amount of tax owed for a given income. It takes into account various deductions and tax credits. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

income.description: The total income of the individual for the year in dollars. This is a float type value.

filing_status.description: The tax filing status of the individual.

deductions.description: The total amount of deductions the individual is claiming in dollars. This is a float type value.

tax_credits.description: The total amount of tax credits the individual is claiming in dollars. This is a float type value.

state.description: The state in which the individual resides, used for determining state-specific taxes.

message.content:
Here’s a very quick “ball‑park” estimate based on the most common scenario—**a single filer who took only the standard deduction and had no additional credits or itemized deductions**.  
(If you’re married filing jointly, head of household, have significant itemized deductions, or qualify for specific credits, let me know so I can adjust the numbers.)

---

### Federal Income Tax Estimate – FY 2023  

| Step | Calculation | Amount |
|------|-------------|--------|
| **Gross income** | — | \$85,000 |
| **Standard deduction (Single)** | — | \-\$12,950 |
| **Adjusted gross income (AGI)** | 85,000 – 12,950 | \$72,050 |
| **Taxable income** | AGI minus personal exemption (none in 2023) | \$72,050 |

#### Applying the 2023 U.S. federal brackets (for Single filers)

| Bracket | Rate | Portion taxed at this rate | Tax from portion |
|---------|------|----------------------------|------------------|
| Up to \$11,000 | 10% | \$11,000 | \$1,100 |
| Next \$33,725 (\$44,725 – \$11,000) | 12% | \$33,725 | \$4,047 |
| Remaining \$27,325 (\$72,050 – \$44,725) | 22% | \$27,325 | \$6,012 |

> **Subtotal:** \$1,100 + \$4,047 + \$6,012 ≈ **\$11,159**

*(Note: These figures use the IRS tables as published for 2023.)*

#### Additional considerations

| Item | Typical impact | Notes |
|------|---------------|-------|
| **Social Security & Medicare payroll taxes** | Separate from income tax (~7.65%) | Usually withheld automatically; not part of the federal income tax figure above. |
| **State/local taxes** | Varies widely | If you live outside New York/New Jersey/etc., your state may impose its own income tax. |
| **Other credits/deductions** | Could reduce liability further | e.g., Child Tax Credit, Earned Income Credit, education credits, mortgage interest, charitable contributions, etc. |

---

### Rough Bottom Line

Assuming nothing else applies beyond the standard deduction:

- **Federal income tax due:** roughly **\$11,200**
- **Payroll taxes (SS+Medicare):** approximately **\$5,175** (7.65% × \$85,000)
- **Estimated total tax burden:** around **\$16,375** before any state taxes or additional credits.

---

#### Want a More Precise Number?

To get an exact figure tailored to your situation, please share:

1. Your **filing status** (e.g., single, married filing jointly).
2. Any **itemized deductions** you plan to claim (mortgage interest, medical expenses, charitable donations, etc.).
3. Whether you qualify for any **tax credits** (Child Tax Credit, Education Credits, Energy Efficiency Credits, etc.).
4. Which **state** you reside in (so we can factor in state income tax).

Once I have those details, I’ll run through the full calculations—including all applicable brackets, credits, and state adjustments—for you!
